```{r}
tn <- raw |>
  filter(patient_state == "TN") |>
  summarise(across(c(N02, Ozone, PM25), ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))

aq_fill <- tribble(
  ~patient_state, ~PM25_fill, ~Ozone_fill, ~N02_fill, ~fill_source,
  "HI",   4.23,       27.5,        2.6,       "HI DOH 2024 annual report (Oahu SLAMS)",
  "AK",   1.34,       36.78,       22.26,     "AK DEC Chickaloon sensor, winter 2024-25",
  "TN",   tn$PM25,    tn$Ozone,    tn$N02,    "TN state mean"
)

df <- df |>
  left_join(aq_fill, by = "patient_state") |>
  mutate(
    aq_imputed = is.na(PM25) & !is.na(PM25_fill),
    aq_source  = if_else(aq_imputed, fill_source, "original"),
    PM25  = coalesce(PM25,  PM25_fill),
    Ozone = coalesce(Ozone, Ozone_fill),
    N02   = coalesce(N02,   N02_fill)
  ) |>
  select(-ends_with("_fill"), -fill_source)

colSums(is.na(df[c("N02", "Ozone", "PM25")]))
count(df, aq_source)
```

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Missingness — look before deciding what to drop or impute
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
# Check the raw insurance labels before recoding them
raw %>% count(payer_type)

cat_vars <- c("patient_race", "payer_type", "patient_state", "region", "division",
              "breast_cancer_diagnosis_code", "metastatic_cancer_diagnosis_code")

clean <- raw %>%
  select(-any_of(c(
    "patient_gender",                        
    "breast_cancer_diagnosis_desc",         
    "metastatic_first_novel_treatment",     
    "metastatic_first_novel_treatment_type"   
  ))) %>%
  mutate(
    payer_type = case_when(
      str_detect(str_to_upper(payer_type), "MEDICAID")   ~ "Medicaid",
      str_detect(str_to_upper(payer_type), "COMMERCIAL") ~ "Commercial",
      str_detect(str_to_upper(payer_type), "MEDICARE")   ~ "Medicare",
      TRUE                                               ~ NA_character_
    ),

    across(all_of(cat_vars), ~ factor(replace_na(as.character(.), "Unknown"))),
    # Collapse rare diagnosis codes so every level has enough patients.
    # This also prevents the train/test column mismatch the tutorial fixes by hand.
    breast_cancer_diagnosis_code     = fct_lump_min(breast_cancer_diagnosis_code,
                                                    min = 20, other_level = "Other"),
    metastatic_cancer_diagnosis_code = fct_lump_min(metastatic_cancer_diagnosis_code,
                                                    min = 20, other_level = "Other"),
    # BMI is mostly missing: keep a flag for "was BMI recorded" before imputing
    bmi_missing = as.integer(is.na(bmi))
  ) %>%
  # Median-impute remaining numeric NAs (BMI + a few zip-level census/air values)
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !any_of(c("patient_id", "DiagPeriodL90D")),
                ~ replace_na(., median(., na.rm = TRUE))))

# Note: when you later split train/test, compute the imputation medians on
# the training split only and apply them to test, to avoid leakage.

stopifnot(!anyNA(clean))
dim(clean)

```

```{r}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Dummy variables (model-ready dataset)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# - patient_state / patient_zip3: too many levels; geography is captured by division
# - region: nested inside division, so it would be redundant
dummy_vars <- c("patient_race", "payer_type", "division",
                "breast_cancer_diagnosis_code", "metastatic_cancer_diagnosis_code")

model_df <- clean %>%
  select(-patient_id, -patient_state, -patient_zip3, -region) %>%
  dummy_cols(select_columns          = dummy_vars,
             remove_first_dummy      = TRUE,   # avoids perfect collinearity
             remove_selected_columns = TRUE) %>% # drops the original factor columns
  clean_names() %>%                            # "patient_race_African American" -> snake_case
  rename(DiagPeriodL90D = diag_period_l90d)

dim(model_df)
stopifnot(all(map_lgl(model_df, is.numeric)))

write_csv(clean,    "clean_data/training_clean.csv")    # cleaned, factors intact (for EDA)
write_csv(model_df, "clean_data/training_model.csv")    # all-numeric, ready for classification

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. EDA — quantitative summaries (tutorial steps)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outcome balance
clean %>% tabyl(DiagPeriodL90D)

# Summary of zip-level population and density
summary(clean[, c("population", "density")])

# Patients per state
table(clean$patient_state)

# Mean population and density by region
clean %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(population = mean(population), density = mean(density), n = n())

# Factor version of the outcome for plotting
eda <- clean %>%
  mutate(DiagPeriodL90D = factor(DiagPeriodL90D, levels = c(0, 1)))

outcome_labels <- c(`0` = "DiagPeriodL90D = 0 (more than 90 days)",
                    `1` = "DiagPeriodL90D = 1 (within 90 days)")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Figure 1 — Median age of zip code by outcome (kernel density)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
age_centers <- eda %>%
  group_by(DiagPeriodL90D) %>%
  summarise(mean_age_median = mean(age_median))

p_age <- ggplot(eda, aes(x = age_median, color = DiagPeriodL90D)) +
  geom_density(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(data = age_centers,
             aes(xintercept = mean_age_median, color = DiagPeriodL90D),
             linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ DiagPeriodL90D, labeller = as_labeller(outcome_labels)) +
  labs(title = "Median Age of Patient's Zip Code by Diagnosis Period",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = group mean",
       x = "Median age of residents (zip code)", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p_age
ggsave("figures/age_median_density.png", p_age, width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Figure 2 — Insurance type by outcome (bar chart, two panels)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
payer_plot_df <- eda %>%
  filter(payer_type != "Unknown") %>%
  mutate(payer_type = factor(payer_type, levels = c("Medicaid", "Commercial", "Medicare")))

# How many rows were left out because insurance was missing
sum(eda$payer_type == "Unknown")

p_payer <- ggplot(payer_plot_df, aes(x = payer_type, fill = payer_type)) +
  geom_bar() +
  geom_text(stat = "count", aes(label = after_stat(count)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ DiagPeriodL90D, labeller = as_labeller(outcome_labels)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(title = "Insurance Type by Diagnosis Period",
       x = "Insurance type", y = "Number of patients") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p_payer
ggsave("figures/payer_type_by_outcome.png", p_payer, width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)

# Proportions are easier to compare than counts when the groups differ in size
payer_plot_df %>%
  tabyl(payer_type, DiagPeriodL90D) %>%
  adorn_percentages("row") %>%
  adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Figure 3 — Bivariate relationships (scatterplot matrix)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
png("figures/scatterplot_matrix.png", width = 2400, height = 2400, res = 300)
scatterplotMatrix(~ income_household_median + home_ownership +
                    education_bachelors + health_uninsured,
                  data = clean,
                  spread = FALSE, smooth = list(lty = 2),
                  main = "Bivariate Scatter Plot Matrix")
dev.off()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Figure 4 — Correlation plot (selected zip-level + air quality vars)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
corr_vars <- c("patient_age", "bmi", "age_median", "income_household_median",
               "home_ownership", "education_bachelors", "health_uninsured",
               "poverty", "unemployment_rate", "limited_english",
               "ozone", "PM25", "N02", "DiagPeriodL90D")

M <- cor(clean[, corr_vars])

png("figures/corrplot.png", width = 2400, height = 2400, res = 300)
corrplot(M, method = "number", order = "hclust", type = "upper",
         tl.col = "black", number.cex = 0.6)
dev.off()
